entries.title: Optimal winning ply in the transversal achievement game (Guan's sharpness conjecture)

source.authors: Kevin Guan
source.paper: The transversal achievement game on a square grid

entries.summary: For every n >= 4, the second player in the n x n transversal achievement game prevents a first-player win through ply 2n+1 via an (n-2)-matching invariant and an O-transversal counterthreat, proving with Guan's upper bound that the exact optimal winning ply is 2n+3.

entries.title: Connected chordal chord diagrams (Nabergall's Conjecture 8.5)

source.authors: Lukas Nabergall
source.paper: The combinatorics of a tree-like functional equation for connected chord diagrams

entries.summary: For every n >= 1, the number of rooted chord diagrams of size n whose crossing graph is connected and chordal equals C_{n-1}^2 = ((1/n) binom(2n-2, n-1))^2, proved end-to-end in Lean 4 across 14 warning-free modules (NabergallChordalDiagrams.connectedChordalDiagram_card) via clique-boundary sector triangulation, earliest-cut irreducible factorization, and Clebsch–Gordan generating-function extraction.

entries.title: Petr–Turek temperate intersecting families (upper-half proof and exact n <= 8)

source.authors: Jan Petr and Pavel Turek
source.paper: Towards odd-sunflowers: temperate families and lightnings
source.journal: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A 220 (2026)

entries.summary: Proves the sharp lightning upper bound L_k = (1/2) binom(2k, k) + binom(2k, k+1) + binom(2k-1, k+2) for every k >= 2 across the entire upper half of the Boolean cube (whenever at most one member has size < k), establishes an O(N_k / k^2) additive bound on the four central ranks (k >= 6), and proves by exact integer search that the unrestricted maxima on [4], [6], [8] are 7, 26, 98. Unrestricted k >= 5 remains open.

entries.title: Cardoso's subset synchronization conjecture (all weakly oriented circular automata)

source.authors: Ângela Cardoso (thesis); Marek Szykuła (survey)
source.paper: Synchronizing Automata: Open Problems (citing Cardoso, University of Porto PhD Thesis, 2014)

entries.summary: Proves Cardoso's exact ceiling bound B(n,m) = (n-1)^2 - (ceil(n/m)-1)(2n - m*ceil(n/m) - 1) sharply for every synchronizing weakly oriented circular automaton and every nonempty m-subset, removing both the unit-jump and rank-(n-1) restrictions of Cardoso's Theorem 5.7.8 via aggregate interval-growth counting across stage lengths. The general DFA conjecture remains open.

entries.title: Yuan–Parrilo permanent–sphere conjecture (order n <= 4, rank <= 3, and c > 5/6 bound)

source.authors: Chenyang Yuan and Pablo A. Parrilo
source.paper: Maximizing Products of Linear Forms, and The Permanent of Positive Semidefinite Matrices

entries.summary: Proves per(A) <= r(A) for every complex Hermitian positive semidefinite (HPSD) matrix of order n <= 4 and whenever (d)_{n-1} <= n^{n-1} (in particular n >= 2*rank(A) - 2, ruling out all rank <= 3 counterexamples; first open case (n=5, d=4)), and establishes the dimension-free exponential lower bound r(A) >= c^n per(A) with c = e exp(-sum_{j>=0} 2^{-j-1} log(1+2^j)) approx 0.836208 > 5/6 (improving e^{-gamma} approx 0.5615).

entries.title: Kashima–Ozeki odd coloring conjecture (all 4-trees and 5-trees)

source.authors: Masaki Kashima and Kenta Ozeki
source.paper: Odd coloring of k-trees

entries.summary: Proves that every finite 4-tree is odd 6-colorable and every finite 5-tree is odd 7-colorable (both sharp, with no bound on vertex order) via exact integer bitset rooted-forest closure certificates (72 terminal forests for k=4; 917 terminal forests for k=5), settling the Kashima–Ozeki conjecture through k=5. The conjecture remains open for k >= 6.

entries.title: Eggert's 1971 conjecture in characteristic two (Kourovka Notebook 17.52)

source.authors: N. Eggert (annotated by L. S. Kazarin; eds. E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov)
source.paper: The Kourovka Notebook: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory (21st Edition); N. H. Eggert, Pacific J. Math. 36 (1971)

entries.summary: Every finite-dimensional commutative associative nilpotent algebra R over a finite (or any perfect) field k of characteristic two satisfies 2 dim_k R^(2) <= dim_k R with no restrictions on generators, grading, nilpotency class, or dim_k R^(2), proved end-to-end in Lean 4 (EggertNilpotentAlgebra.kourovka_17_52_char_two), resolving the characteristic-two case of Eggert's 1971 conjecture (Kourovka 17.52) and yielding the abelian-factor finite 2-group case of Kourovka 11.44 via Amberg–Kazarin's reduction. Odd primes p remain open.

entries.title: Counterexamples to the Sylvester characterization of linearly presented graded Möbius algebras (Fouli et al., Conjecture 4.1)

source.authors: Louiza Fouli, Sean Grate, Selvi Kara, Adam LaClair, Jason McCullough, Vinh Nguyen, Aleksandra Sobieska, and Prajwal Udanshive
source.paper: Graded Betti numbers of graded Möbius algebras of uniform matroids

entries.summary: Disproves the Sylvester-to-linear-presentation direction of Conjecture 4.1 of Fouli et al. (arXiv:2609.03827v1) via an infinite rank-3 family of quadratic Sylvester matroids indexed by F_2^m (m >= 3, starting at 15 points with beta_{2,4} = 20 and lower bound beta_{2,4} >= 2^{m-2}(2^m-1)(2^m-2)/6) and a 15-point quadratic Steiner triple system with every pair in a unique 3-circuit (beta_{2,4} = 4), each certified over Q by an explicit Koszul 2-cycle and separating boundary-killing functional. Proposition 4.4 of the paper proves the forward direction.

entries.title: Sharpness of the 2|G|^2 square-root overgroup bound (Kourovka Notebook 18.46)

source.authors: Ant. A. Klyachko (citing D. V. Baranov and Ant. A. Klyachko; eds. E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov)
source.paper: The Kourovka Notebook: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory (21st Edition); D. V. Baranov and Ant. A. Klyachko, Siber. Math. J. 53, no. 2 (2012), 201-206

entries.summary: Affirmatively resolves Kourovka Notebook 18.46 (is the bound |H| <= 2|G|^2 sharp?). Lean 4 proves the general upper bound (Kourovka1846.square_overgroup_upper: every finite G embeds in a host of order exactly 2|G|^2 in which every element of G is a square) and sharpness for the dihedral group D_8 (Kourovka1846.D8.card_ge_128: every simultaneous square-root host of D_8 has order >= 128 = 2|D_8|^2), with no CFSG, Burnside or group-catalogue input and zero sorry, kernel-replayed in CI. Independently, a written CFSG proof shows that for every alternating group A_n with n >= 4096, any finite overgroup in which the single element (1 2 3 4)(5 6) has a square root has order at least 2|A_n|^2; Lean formalizes only that argument's final no-root lemma. verify.py exhausts the 16 marked index-two kernels for D_8 and checks the A_4096 witness with mutation controls.

entries.title: Carving-width and elementary-abelian Petersen-lift obstructions to 5-edge-connected 5-regular class 2 multigraphs

source.authors: Yulai Ma, Davide Mattiolo, Eckhard Steffen, and Isaak H. Wolf
source.paper: Pairwise disjoint perfect matchings in r-edge-connected r-regular graphs

entries.summary: Proves that every 5-edge-connected 5-regular loopless multigraph of carving width at most 7 (via 7 parity-allowed port templates across 20,979 oriented joins), as well as every 5-edge-connected F_p^d-voltage lift (p in {2,3,5,7}, d >= 0) of P+M+N for perfect matchings M, N of the Petersen graph P (via exact cubic profiles and 131 verified 50-vertex quintic colorings), is 5-edge-colorable, while edge-connectivity 4 is sharp across cyclic covers of every degree n >= 2 without triple edges. Ma–Mattiolo–Steffen–Wolf Problem 1.6 remains open in general.

entries.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: 5(n-1)/4 upper bound, settlement for n <= 15, and musquash exclusions

source.authors: John H. Conway (recorded by D. R. Woodall, 1971); Dániel Gábor Simon (2026 upper bound)
source.paper: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of 4n/3 (Dániel Gábor Simon, Oct 2026); D. R. Woodall, Thrackles and deadlock (1971)
source.target: Conway's Thrackle Conjecture (m <= n) and Global Edge-Bound Problem

entries.summary: Settles Conway's thrackle conjecture (m <= n) for all graphs on n <= 15 vertices (improving n <= 12) plus four 16-vertex minimal bicyclic obstructions via audited strict-RUP SAT/LRAT refutations, lowers the global upper bound from floor(4(n-1)/3) to floor(5(n-1)/4) for all n >= 5 via zero-curvature discharging (combinatorial discharging and forest reduction formalized in Lean 4), proves 5/4 is the exact sharpness wall of the NSB(16) embedding framework via girth-8 periodic witnesses and a 255-vertex dual showing Theta(1,7,9) necessity, and excludes all distinct cycles of length <= 7 sharing a vertex with any standard odd or Woodall distinct musquash. Conway's full conjecture remains open for general n >= 16.

entries.title: Thompson's cyclic matrix permutation conjecture (Kourovka 16.95): rank-one finite fields and unrestricted GL(5,2)–GL(7,2)

source.authors: J. G. Thompson (eds. E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov)
source.paper: The Kourovka Notebook: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory (21st Edition)

entries.summary: Proves Thompson's cyclic column-ordering conjecture for every invertible rank-one perturbation of a scalar permutation matrix over F_2, F_3, and F_4 in every dimension (with no support restrictions), and over every fixed finite field F_q in all dimensions n >= N(q) via an explicit zero-sum block partition and two-cycle criterion. Independently verifies all unrestricted matrices in GL(5,2) (exact minimum 24 = 4! cyclic orders), GL(6,2) (139,629 orbit-cover representatives), and GL(7,2) (28,892,664 orbit-cover representatives, available via --seven). General rank in arbitrary dimension remains open.

entries.title: Herzog–Schönheim conjecture for all finite almost simple groups (Kourovka 21.93 / Erdős #274)

source.authors: M. Herzog and J. Schönheim (annotated by L. Margolis; eds. E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov)
source.paper: The Kourovka Notebook: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory (21st Edition); Erdős Problem #274

entries.summary: Proves the Herzog–Schönheim conjecture (Kourovka 21.93 / Erdős #274) for every finite almost simple group S <= G <= Aut(S), overcoming Garonzi–Margolis Remark 5.1 (unbounded reciprocal index sums) via a filled-fibre capacity criterion K(m) D(N) < 1 (counting step formalized in Lean 4) combined with CFSG and exact rational verification across all classical, exceptional, alternating, sporadic, and Tits families (complementing Menon's Nov 2026 solvable proof). General non-almost-simple nonsolvable groups remain open.

entries.title: 2-degenerate linear arboricity conjecture (Basavaraju et al., Conjecture 2): odd-cycle packing, paired neighborhoods, mad(G) <= 3, and 9-vertex sharpness

source.authors: Manu Basavaraju, Arijit Bishnu, Mathew Francis, and Drimit Pattanayak
source.paper: The linear arboricity conjecture for graphs of low degeneracy

entries.summary: Partially resolves Basavaraju–Bishnu–Francis–Pattanayak Conjecture 2 (2-linear colorability of 2-degenerate graphs with Delta <= 4): proves 2-linear colorability (at most 1 defect) when G has no two edge-disjoint odd cycles, proves prescribed-pair defect flexibility whenever every degree-4 neighborhood has a perfect matching (covering all claw-free 2-degenerate graphs and iterated twin-cap, pendant-triangle, long-ear, and double-subdivision closures), settles the density equality endpoint mad(G) <= 3 for all subquartic graphs (extending J.-L. Wu's 1999 strict mad(G) < 3 bound), and proves sharpness of the |E| >= 2|V|-5 one-defect threshold via a 9-vertex, 12-edge graph forcing exactly 2 defects (formalized in Lean 4) plus infinite families forcing (2|V|-|E|)/3 defects. The unrestricted 2-degenerate Delta <= 4 conjecture remains open.

entries.title: Disproof of Gaetz–Gao's strong hull property conjecture for Coxeter groups (Conjecture 1.2)

source.authors: Christian Gaetz and Yibo Gao
source.paper: The hull metric on Coxeter groups

entries.summary: Unconditionally disproves Gaetz–Gao Conjecture 1.2 (both the strong hull property and the weaker ordinary hull property, showing log |Conv(-,-)| is not a metric on Coxeter groups in general) in the affine Coxeter group W(A3~), formalized end-to-end in Lean 4 on Mathlib's presented Coxeter group via an exact l1-isometry into Z^6 and two-point Phi-box theorem (422 theorems, zero sorry, standard axioms only). Exact zero-float computation also verifies minimal counterexamples (60*121 = 7260 < 7921 ordinary; 96*97 = 9312 < 9825 strong), and the written proof extends the disproof to every irreducible affine Coxeter group of rank >= 4 (completing the affine dichotomy with Liu's 2025 rank-3 proof).

entries.title: Gessel–Zhuang Conjecture 7.1 (inverse peak real-rootedness): all 7 families at every fixed count and unconditional first mixed rows

source.authors: Ira M. Gessel and Yan Zhuang
source.paper: Two-sided permutation statistics via symmetric functions

entries.summary: Proves eventual real-rootedness (all zeros real, nonpositive, and simple for non-elementary rows) for every part (a)-(g) of Gessel-Zhuang Conjecture 7.1 at every fixed conditioning count k for all sufficiently large n >= N(k) via triangular generating-function extraction and Popov-Sedletskii Mittag-Leffler root localization. Independently proves unconditional real-rootedness at every n >= 1 for all elementary rows (r <= 2) and for the first non-elementary mixed rows ((a)-(d) at k = 1 and (e)-(g) at k = 3) by explicit n >= 40 trigonometric error bounds plus exact zero-float integer Sturm-chain certification through n = 39. Uniform-in-k real-rootedness for all pairs (n, k) remains open.

entries.title: Tuza's 1981 conjecture: universal bound 14*tau(G) <= 39*nu(G) and colored-family bound 21/8

source.authors: Zsolt Tuza (1981); Sichen Wang (2026 baseline)
source.paper: A Bound Below 2.8 for Tuza's Conjecture (Sichen Wang, Sept 2026); Z. Tuza, Graphs and Combinatorics 6 (1990), 373-380
source.target: Tuza's Conjecture (tau(G) <= 2*nu(G)) and Universal Constant Bound

entries.summary: Proves the universal bound 14*tau(G) <= 39*nu(G) (tau(G) <= (39/14)*nu(G) approx 2.7857*nu(G)) for every finite simple graph G via simultaneous triangle-book rotation on distinct red opposites, safe opposite switching, and a 6-inequality rational cover certificate—improving both Sichen Wang's Sept 2026 record (165/59 approx 2.7966, arXiv:2609.13831v1) and Tyler B. Hughes's Nov 2026 unrefereed draft (81/29 approx 2.7931). Also proves the sharper red-blue colored-family bound 8*tau_R(G) + 5*|private| <= 21*nu_R(G) (21/8 = 2.625 < 8/3). Formalized end-to-end in Lean 4 on Mathlib's SimpleGraph (552 theorems, zero sorry, standard axioms only, MIT-licensed adaptation of Wang's tuza-lean base). Partially resolves Tuza's conjecture by lowering the universal constant; tau(G) <= 2*nu(G) remains open.

entries.title: Tuza's conjecture for five-vertex bipartizers and sharp near-Mantel density threshold (e(G) >= n^2/4 - 3n + C)

source.authors: Zhen Liu and Qinghou Zeng
source.paper: Tuza's conjecture for graphs with at least n^2/4 - cn edges
source.target: Conjecture 1.1 (Tuza's Conjecture) and Theorem 1.2 (near-Mantel density threshold)

entries.summary: Proves Tuza's inequality tau(G) <= 2*nu(G) unconditionally for every finite simple graph G admitting a vertex set S of size |S| <= 5 such that G - S is bipartite (no density or codegree assumption), via weak König-Egerváry link reductions, a Hall-type star reduction, Galvin list edge-coloring, and five-vertex core analysis. As a corollary, improves the near-Mantel edge-density threshold of Liu and Zeng (arXiv:2610.15539v1, Oct 2026) from c < 2 to every fixed c < 3, sharpens the endpoint to e(G) >= n^2/4 - 3n + C with C = binom(693600, 2) + 349 for sufficiently large n, and establishes the quantization law n^2/4 - jn/2 + O(1) for the maximum edge count of large counterexamples in terms of the least bipartization number j (with j >= 6 if any counterexample exists). Supplementary exact finite checks in verify.py exhaust all 1,024 five-vertex cores, 1,099 small links, and 16,589 boundary Hall shapes plus 2 rejected mutations. Universal Tuza's conjecture, |S| = 6, and C = 0 remain open.

entries.title: Gaetz–Gao Coxeter balance constants: full classification of 1/3 fully commutative equality heaps and uniform 1/8 convex bound

source.authors: Christian Gaetz and Yibo Gao
source.paper: Balance constants for Coxeter groups
source.journal: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 376 (2023), 8973-9000
source.target: Question 3.10 and Theorem 1.4 / Table 1 (uniform balance lower bounds)

entries.summary: Completely classifies all fully commutative intervals achieving the sharp 1/3 balance constant across every finite Coxeter group of every rank (settling Gaetz-Gao Question 3.10, Trans. AMS 2023): up to componentwise order duality (which is necessary, as reversing the Figure 2 word in D_4 shows), the connected equality heaps are precisely P_2, P_4, and P_7, proved via a log-concave four-column path obstruction reducing every classical rank to B_5/D_5 plus exact zero-float enumeration of all fully commutative elements in B_5, D_5, E_6, E_7, E_8, F_4, G_2, H_3, H_4 (with the local four-column counting core formalized in Lean 4). For arbitrary nonsingleton geodesically convex sets in finite Coxeter groups, proves the uniform lower bound b(C) >= 1/8 (improving Gaetz-Gao's 1/(2e^{12})), including b(C) >= 1/3 in every rank-3 non-triangle Coxeter system (such as H_3) and b(C) >= 1/(2e^{7/6}) in all types D_r (improving 1/(2e^4)). The general 1/3-2/3 balance conjecture for arbitrary convex sets (Conjecture 1.2) remains open.

entries.title: Marcus–de Oliveira 1973 determinantal conjecture: universal U(4) to SO(4) reduction, all-order one-outlier & rank-excess-2 theorems, and exact compound-polytope obstructions

source.authors: Marvin Marcus (1973); Graciano N. de Oliveira (1982); Kijti Rodtes (2020)
source.paper: Derivations, Plücker relations, and the numerical range (Indiana Univ. Math. J. 22, 1972/73); Normal matrices (Linear Multilinear Algebra 12, 1982); A class of normal dilation matrices affirming the Marcus-de Oliveira conjecture (Rodtes, 2020)
source.target: Marcus–de Oliveira Determinantal Conjecture: det(A + B) in conv{prod_i (a_i + b_{sigma(i)})}

entries.summary: Six-pillar structural advance on the 1973 Marcus–de Oliveira Determinantal Conjecture (MOC): (A) proves MOC for all n when sigma(A) lies on a generalized circle and sigma(B) has at most one outlier off a second generalized circle — settling n = 4 whenever either spectrum is concyclic (including Hermitian A + arbitrary normal B) and extending Shitov (2025) to Hermitian A + at most 4 nonreal eigenvalues of B for all n; (B) proves all-n rank-excess-2 (rank(A - cI) + rank(B + cI) <= n + 2, closing rank (4,4) at n = 6) and all n = 4 cross-spectral collisions; (C) proves the universal U(4) -> SO(4) simultaneous 70-minor real-chord reduction conv Delta_{U(4)}(a,b) = conv Delta_{SO(4)}(a,b) without constraining either spectrum; (D) certifies a continuous disjoint doubly-nonconcyclic n = 4 two-tetrahedron family over all U(4) via a 151-SOS rational atlas alongside 48-vertex Shor/P(delta) obstructions and escaped KKT saddles; (E) classifies collision-free singular boundaries with inward transverse Hessian for all n; and (F) computes the exact 82-facet Pi_4 polytope, sharp O(4) = U(4) Orbit-2 breach gamma approx -0.1348845 via 23-square Q(rho) SOS, Klein-four V_4 protection for all 4x4 complex Hadamard matrices, and Tao's 6x6 Hadamard 45-zero Pi_6 escape (exact l_inf distance 1/40) with positive spectral slices. Accompanied by a 13-module, 454-theorem Lean 4 helper/structural suite (including end-to-end Lean proofs of n = 4 collision, all-n PGL_2(C) invariance, V_4 Hadamard protection, Pi_4 facet witness, Tao 6x6 obstruction, and n = 4 arrowhead eigenbasis law) and exact zero-float verify.py across all 7 sections. The unrestricted conjecture remains open for n >= 4.

entries.title: Erdős Problem #86 ($100): hypercube C4-free edge density pi_e(C4) <= 0.59145, breaking Baber's 2012 bound 0.60318, with sharp finite bounds ex(Q8,C4) <= 684 and ex(Q9,C4) <= 1536

source.authors: Paul Erdős (1984, 1990, 1991); Rahil Baber (2012)
source.paper: Erdős Problem #86 (erdosproblems.com/86); Baber, Turán densities of hypercubes (arXiv:1201.3587)
source.target: Is every C4-free subgraph of Q_n of size at most (1/2 + o(1)) n 2^(n-1)? Equivalently pi_e(C4) = 1/2.

entries.summary: Proves the new asymptotic bound pi_e(C4) <= 253730158483485323/429000000000000000 = 0.591445... < 0.59145, improving Baber's 2012 flag-algebra record 0.603173 that stood for 14 years, via a coupled full-Q4 + rooted-B5 + finite-lattice-cut + edge-book inventory dual certificate replayed in exact rationals. The same framework gives six new finite bounds ex(Q8,C4) <= 684 (lower bound 682), ex(Q9,C4) <= 1536 (lower bound 1532), ex(Q10,C4) <= 3369, ex(Q11,C4) <= 7379, ex(Q12,C4) <= 16072, ex(Q16,C4) <= 337372, all strictly below iterated facet averaging from ex(Q7,C4) = 304. Exact primal SDP floors show pure full-Q4 flag algebra cannot go below 692 on Q8, so the higher couplings are necessary; three structural obstructions (odd-dimension 3-edge-defect, 3x3-block Hamilton-fibre obstruction on Q9, exact period <= 16 translation-invariant extrema 296/672/1472/3200 on Q7..Q10) restrict non-odd-square escapes. Flag-algebra soundness and the obstruction theorems are formalized in two Lean 4 modules (80 kernel-checked theorems); exact zero-float verify.py replays all certificates with corrupted-certificate mutation rejection. The conjecture pi_e(C4) = 1/2 remains open.

entries.title: Barranca's Conjecture 2.1.2: the only graphs recognizable by spectrum as induced subgraphs are K1, 2K1, K2, K3 and P3

source.authors: Emily Barranca
source.paper: Recognizing Induced Subgraph and Tree Structure from the Adjacency Spectrum of a Graph (Ph.D. dissertation, University of Rhode Island, 2024)
source.target: Conjecture 2.1.2 (p. 26): K1, 2K1, K2, K3 and P3 are the only graphs recognizable by spectrum (Definition 2.1.1)

entries.summary: Proves Barranca's conjecture in full: among nonempty finite simple graphs, exactly K1, 2K1, K2, K3 and P3 have the property that adjacency-cospectral hosts always agree on containing them as induced subgraphs. An integral spectral trade (every integral-spectrum graph plus cliques/stars/isolates is cospectral with a union of cliques and stars), applied to the F_2^n Cayley hull of any pattern, excludes every connected pattern other than cliques and stars; explicit cospectral pairs exclude K_m (m >= 4) and K_{1,m} (m >= 3); an induced-embedding cancellation lemma reduces disconnected patterns to ten explicit seed pairs on at most 8 vertices, checked by exact integer characteristic polynomials and induced-injection search in verify.py (with mutation controls); and the five positive cases follow from trace counts and positive semidefiniteness of A + I on unions of cliques.

entries.title: Guralnick–Tong-Viet–Tracey Baer–Suzuki variations: prime-order commutator criterion for O_p(G) (Conjecture 2) proved; Engel-product criterion (Conjecture 1) proved at p = 2 and for PSL2/PGL2

source.authors: Robert M. Guralnick, Hung P. Tong-Viet, Gareth Tracey
source.paper: Weakly subnormal subgroups and variations of the Baer-Suzuki theorem (J. London Math. Soc. (2) 111 (2025), e70057)
source.target: Conjecture 2 (conjD): x of prime order p with every [x,g] trivial or p-singular lies in O_p(G); Conjecture 1 (multicommutators)

entries.summary: Theorem A proves Conjecture 2 in full: if x has prime order p in a finite group G and x is not in O_p(G), some commutator [x,g] is nontrivial of order prime to p. The key new step is a lifting lemma for class products through a normal odd p-subgroup with cyclic Sylow quotient, proved via the class multiplication formula and a scalar-action lemma (an odd normal p-subgroup acts by scalars in any irreducible character nonvanishing on an invariably generating pair, via an explicit class-two orbit basis), applied to the quotient-level selection in GTT's minimal-counterexample reduction. Theorem B proves Conjecture 1 (products of k-fold Engel commutators all p-elements implies x in O_p(G)) for p = 2 in every finite group, and for G = PSL2(q) or PGL2(q) at every p, via a nonsplit-torus trace test and Baer's Engel theorem; the residual A6 / M10 case is an exact finite lemma over all 1440 automorphisms of A6 checked in verify.py with mutation controls. Conjecture 1 remains open in general at odd primes.

entries.title: Alspach's 1988 orthogonal matching problem: a full rainbow matching exists once N >= 2d + C log d / log log d (sublogarithmic vertex surplus)

source.authors: Brian Alspach (1988); Michelle Delcourt, Luke Postle
source.paper: Finding an almost perfect matching in a hypergraph avoiding forbidden submatchings (J. London Math. Soc., DOI 10.1112/jlms.70660), Conjecture 2.12; Alspach, Problem 89, Discrete Math. 69 (1988)
source.target: Conjecture 2.12 (Alspach): a simple 2d-regular graph edge-coloured so that each colour class is a 2-factor has a full rainbow matching

entries.summary: Proves that for absolute constants C, d0 and every d >= d0, any simple graph on N >= 2d + C log d / log log d vertices that is the edge-disjoint union of d spanning 2-factors has a matching using exactly one edge from every factor, improving the surplus d^{3/4+o(1)} (Munhá Correia–Pokrovskiy–Sudakov, Theorem 1.5) and the remarked d^{1/2+o(1)}. The proof randomly orients every factor cycle, takes a random cut with exactly d tails, and exchanges the roles of factors and arc heads so that factors and tails form two classes of size d while the surplus vertices become surplus colours; a one-sided-codegree version of Keevash–Pokrovskiy–Sudakov–Yepremyan Theorem 4.1 (justified step by step, since lower codegrees can genuinely fail, as a twin-clone example shows) then gives a perfect rainbow matching. verify.py exactly checks the role exchange, shadow moments and negative controls on small instances. Alspach's conjecture without any surplus (N >= 2d + 1) remains open.

entries.title: Stanley–Zanello Conjecture 1.1(iv): generalized Reiner–Stanton q-binomial differences are eventually nonnegative and unimodal for every k >= 5, with exactly one exceptional b

source.authors: Richard P. Stanley, Fabrizio Zanello
source.paper: A generalization of a 1998 unimodality conjecture of Reiner and Stanton (J. Combin. 11 (2020), 111-126)

entries.summary: For every fixed k >= 5 there is a threshold M(k) such that for all m >= M and every admissible b (k-2 <= b <= (km-4k+4)/(k-2), k(m-b) even), f(k,m,b) = [m choose k]_q - q^(k(m-b)/2+b-2k+2) [b choose k-2]_q is nonnegative and unimodal if and only if b != (km-4k+2)/(k-2). Previously known only for k = 5 (Stanley–Zanello) and k = 6, 7 (Koutschan–Uncu–Wong, arXiv:2302.04067). The proof bounds the first difference of the subtracted Gaussian polynomial by 2^h (1+n)^(h-2) uniformly in b and the shift, compares against the growth of the first difference of [m choose k]_q on the half-range (using symmetry), and shows the shift-one exception is never unimodal. Formalized end-to-end in Lean 4 as ReinerStanton.stanley_zanello_iv (both directions, uniform in b; zero sorry, kernel-replayed in CI); verify.py checks the classification exactly for k = 3..10 against q-Pascal coefficient arrays with mutation controls. Sporadic failures for small m are not classified.

entries.title: Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture proved for all n >= 7k (Lean 4), Milojević–Sudakov Conjectures 1 and 3 resolved on [0, 1/3], and exact k = 8 certificates including g(33,8) = C(32,7)

source.authors: N. Manickam, D. Miklós, N. M. Singhi (1988); A. Chowdhury, G. Sarkis, S. Shahriari; A. Milojević, B. Sudakov
source.paper: A New Quadratic Bound for the Manickam-Miklós-Singhi Conjecture (arXiv:1403.1844v4); On the Probability a Weighted Bernoulli Sum Exceeds Its Mean (arXiv:2606.30287v1)
source.target: MMS Conjecture (conj:MMS, n >= 4k); Milojević–Sudakov Conjecture 1 (conj:prob) and Conjecture 3 (q:MMS_variant)

entries.summary: Pillar I (Lean 4, end-to-end): for every n >= 7k and every real n-vector with nonnegative sum, at least C(n-1,k-1) of its k-subsets have nonnegative sum (ManickamMiklosSinghi.mms_seven_k), improving the best linear bound n > 10^46 k (Pokrovskiy 2015) and the quadratic bound n >= 8k^2 (Chowdhury–Sarkis–Shahriari); the full conjectured range n >= 4k remains open. Pillar II: resolves Milojević–Sudakov (June 2026) Conjecture 1 — P(sum w_i v_i >= p) >= p for positive weights summing to one, i.i.d. Bernoulli(p), all p in [0, 1/3] (sharp at 1/3 by their Proposition) — and Conjecture 3 (bounded-support restricted MMS for n >= (3+eps)k), with [0, 1/7] and unit fractions (after Alon–Emek–Feldman–Tennenholtz 2013) formalized in Lean 4 and [1/7, 1/3) certified by exact zero-float integer/int128 replay plus compactness transfer; compared against Barritz's bounded-support surplus preprint (Zenodo, Oct 2026). Pillar III: exact k = 8 frontier — f(8) >= 26 via an explicit witness (Lean), Farkas certificates for g(18,8), g(28,8), g(30,8), g(32,8), and a new spectral certificate for g(33,8) = C(32,7) = 3,365,856; residue classes n = 2, 3, 5, 7 mod 8 below 56 remain open. 32-module Lean 4 suite kernel-replayed in CI; verify.py replays all certificates with mutation rejection.

entries.title: Willems's conjecture (Kourovka Notebook 21.91) at p = 3: the squared degrees of the irreducible 3-Brauer characters of every finite group sum to at least |G|_{3'}

source.authors: W. Willems (communicated by G. Malle; eds. E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov)
source.paper: The Kourovka Notebook: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory (21st Edition), Problem 21.91; G. Malle, On Willems' conjecture on Brauer character degrees (Adv. Math. 380 (2021), 107609)

entries.summary: Proves Willems's conjecture at the prime 3: for every finite group G, the sum of the squares of the degrees of the irreducible 3-modular Brauer characters is at least the 3'-part of |G| (previously known only at p = 2, by Malle 2021). Via Tong-Viet's reduction to quasisimple groups with a prescribed faithful central character, the proof (i) completes the defining-characteristic Lie-type cases at every prime by tensoring the Steinberg module with a small fundamental module and bounding a simple quotient's degree; (ii) settles the ordinary and spin sectors of alternating groups at p = 3 using two staircase partitions of 3-defect zero with an effective infinite tail, a degree-sum transfer inequality between ranks, and cyclic-defect block bounds for the remaining finite ranks; and (iii) checks A7, 2.A8, 2.A9 from the GAP character table library. As a by-product the projective inequality holds for all covers of finite simple groups of Lie type at all primes. verify.py replays all finite interval and degree certificates in exact integer arithmetic with negative controls; Lean 4 formalizes only the tensor-quotient degree lemma. The conjecture for p >= 5 remains open.
